item.title: Indiana man builds 60,000-gallon backyard water park
item.description: Cory Johnson of Cromwell decided to elevate his backyard experience, opting for a private water park after a frustratingly long pool installation wait. His dream evolved from a basic pool design, famously sketched on a napkin, into a spectacular 60,000-gallon water park featuring special attractions. With rentals at $140 per hour and a steady stream of bookings, he's also eyeing future upgrades like a steam cave and relaxing hot spring.

item.title: 10-year-old New Jersey girl writes poem on Colombian heritage, makes it to Top 10 in poetry contest
item.description: A 10-year-old girl from New Jersey has been named among the Top 10 winners of Creative Communication’s national poetry contest. Luisa Gonzalez’s poem, All Stitched Together, was selected from thousands of entries. Inspired by the Colombian flag, the poem reflects her cultural identity and pride in her heritage. She had previously received honourable mentions in the competition.

item.title: Barbra Streisand’s $10 million gift helps women’s heart centre treat 1,700 patients annually
item.description: Barbra Streisand's generous donation of $10 million to Cedars-Sinai has paved the way for the creation of the Women’s Heart Center. This groundbreaking facility aims to delve into the disparities in cardiovascular health among women, addressing unique diagnostic and treatment challenges. Annually, over 1,700 women benefit from specialized cardiac care, emphasizing tailored medical approaches for heart disease, ultimately showcasing the critical need for research in women's health.
item.dc:creator: TOI World Desk

item.title: At 11, UK-based Aneeshwar Kunchala to receive Junior Jane Goodall Earth Medal for wildlife conservation
item.description: Aneeshwar Kunchala, a passionate young wildlife educator, is set to receive the prestigious Junior Jane Goodall Earth Medal in 2026. His journey into conservation began at just four years old when he learned about the devastating effects of plastic on whales. Celebrated for his remarkable contributions to wildlife advocacy through media, he has initiated citizen science projects and engaging educational presentations that inspire children to connect with nature.

item.title: California students invented a cooling device for firefighters and farmworkers
item.description: Students at Calistoga Junior/Senior High School developed a cooling device targeting hot working conditions. They presented their invention at EurekaFest and the California State Capitol. The project utilized a $7,500 grant from the InvenTeams initiative to support their research and development. Their invention gained recognition as a finalist for the SXSW Innovation Awards. The InvenTeams program aims to inspire students to address real-world problems through practical inventions.

item.title: Jack Dorsey’s $31.9 million San Francisco homes: A renovation that has dragged on for 14 years
item.description: Twitter co-founder Jack Dorsey has made bold moves in the real estate market, acquiring two stunning properties in the upscale Sea Cliff neighborhood of San Francisco. His first investment of $9.99 million sparked an extensive redevelopment that aims to create a serene wellness retreat, prioritizing privacy and a connection to nature. Following this, he invested $21.9 million in a neighboring property, expanding his sanctuary amidst the ongoing renovation's intricate progress.
item.dc:creator: TOI Real Estate Desk

item.title: Joni Mitchell US Citizenship: Music icon finally becomes American; can now vote
item.description: At 82, Joni Mitchell, the iconic Canadian singer-songwriter, has officially become a United States citizen. She shared her joyous moment of naturalization via social media, reminiscing about her journey since moving to the US in 1965. This milestone not only recognizes her profound impact on American music but also grants her the privilege of voting in US elections, solidifying her bond with the country she has long called home.

item.title: From $40 To Global Brand: Daymond John turns side hustle into FUBU empire; family and hip-hop drive rise
item.description: Daymond John started FUBU with a small investment and his mother's support in the early 1990s. He sold handmade hats in Queens and quickly generated significant sales, showing demand for the brand. After facing multiple rejections from banks, his mother provided financial backing through a second mortgage. Collaborating with musicians like LL Cool J helped boost the brand's visibility and credibility.

item.title: UK dad spent £80,000 building an 80-square-metre tropical garden hideout
item.description: A father from Milton Keynes transformed his garden into a tropical retreat featuring an aquarium and exotic animals. He spent over £80,000 building the 80-square-metre space as a personal escape from daily life. Initially, his wife and neighbors were skeptical but grew to appreciate his vision. His children also enjoy the garden, helping feed the Koi fish and exploring the space.

item.title: Children Honoured For Bravery: 5-year-old leads sister to safety; officials hail response
item.description: In a remarkable display of bravery, a five-year-old boy named Hudson Tenn from Michigan sprang into action during a medical emergency involving his grandmother. Recognizing her need for help, he took the initiative to leave their house with his younger sister. Fortunately, kind-hearted neighbors noticed the children and promptly summoned emergency services, ensuring his grandmother received critical medical care in a timely manner.
item.dc:creator: TOI World Desk

item.title: UK collector's £20 car boot sale find: 47 rare Superman comics sell for £63,440 after years in loft
item.description: A collector's chance find at a car boot sale led to a remarkable discovery when he purchased a box of comics for £20, only to unearth rare Superman editions hidden away in his loft for years. Following some online research during the pandemic, he confirmed that these gems, originally commissioned for a family bar mitzvah in 1988, could fetch a stunning £63,440 at auction.
item.dc:creator: TOI World Desk

item.title: Inside Meryl Streep’s former five-storey New York townhouse built in 1845
item.description: Meryl Streep’s former Greenwich Village townhouse, built in 1845, combines historic architecture with luxury features, including six fireplaces, six bedrooms and a rooftop garden. The three-time Oscar winner owned the five-storey New York property from 1995 to 2005. In 2016, it returned to the market with its asking price reduced to $28.5 million.
